newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus markets settle back in sluggish mood.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus markets settle back in sluggish mood.

text.p: Little movement was registered on the Cyprus stock market during the week with the general index just slightly down.
The CSE general index closed at 81.53 points on Wednesday down from 81.83 when it closed on Friday.
"The depression appears to be at its limits," said broker Christodoulos Ellinas from Share Link. "I think movement will be steady and by sector from now on."
Banking stocks, the strongest on the exchange, closed at 90.07 on Wednesday, a slight drop from Friday's close of 90.20.
Fully paid shares in the Bank of Cyprus closed on Wednesday at 339 from 341.5 on Friday. Fully paid shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank gained 2.5 cents, closing at 324.
Hellenic Bank fully paid shares closed at 257.5 on Wednesday, shedding two cents from their closing price on Friday, while shares in the Universal Savings Bank lost two cents to close at 138.
National carrier Cyprus Airways scored another year low of 0.376 cents on Wednesday, continuing its downward trend which started last month.

Strained relations with its employees and future strategies to get the airline out of the red are due to come under the microscope of the House of Representatives financial affairs committee on Friday. Cyprus Airways is 80 percent state controlled.

Stocks in insurance companies fell. The sub-index closed at 56.67 on Wednesday from Friday's close of 57.22. Universal Life insurance closed the day at 373, down 6.5 cents from last week. Paneuropean Insurance lost 1.5 cents and closed at 121. Interamerican closed at 99.5, registering a 3.5 drop from Friday.
Vassiliko Cement, target of a massive share purchase by Italian Italcementi last week was trading at 165.5 on Wednesday from 168.5 on Friday.
Italcementi and Vassiliko have clinched a deal whereby Italcementi will raise its stake in the Cypriot company to 33 percent from its current holding of 20 percent.
The matter currently rests with the Central Bank of Cyprus, which has to approve all foriegn investment in Cyprus.
The Cyprus Cement Company has challenged the deal between Vassiliko and Italcementi.
It says a majority shareholder in Vassiliko, Greek Orthodox Archbishop Chrysostomos, reneged on a 'gentleman's agreement' to sell the bulk of the shares to them.
